Re: Implement saveAsTextFile() in the RDD class

I've looked at the recent work on `saveAsTextFile()` - glad to see progress being made here!

It appears that the current approach is to serialize to a string on the R side rather than Java. If we want to do that, it would be most useful if we can represent any arbitrary R object as a record in the text file. I modified the "saveAsTextFile" branch for this feature to do so.

I removed `toString()`, whose purpose in R is for printing, and will very quickly get us into trouble (anything outside of simple types, character vectors with newline characters in them, etc.), and replaced it with a base64 encoding of the a raw serialized representation of the object.

I also added a function `textObjectFile()`, which behaves like `textFile()`, except that it also deserializes the data so that you are dealing with your native R objects again.

I also added a unit test to illustrate how it is used and expected to behave. I don't know if this is what you have in mind, but it's moving toward the type of thing I've been looking for - a way to permanently store results of analysis (including more complex R objects) that may be too large to `collect()` in a way that I can load back in as an RDD exactly the way it was before I wrote it.

Since I'm not familiar with your PR protocol, and since I did this without discussing and it may not be exactly what you want, I'll provide a link to the code comparison instead of a PR:

https://github.com/hafen/SparkR-pkg/compare/sun-rui:saveAsTextFile...saveAsTextFile-serialize

I'm happy to PR and discuss changes from there.

Re: Implement saveAsTextFile() in the RDD class

Hi, Thanks for your opinion
saveAsTextFile() is intended to behave like RDD.saveAsTextFile() in Spark, which saves the RDD as a text file, using string representations of elements. The text file can be read by other applications that can accept text input format. While the base64 encoding of the a raw serialized representation of the R object can only be recognized by SparkR again.

To satisfy your demand, we can implement saveAsObjectFile() as defined in Spark. It can save the RDD as a SequenceFile of serialized R objects. we need also implement objectFile() in SparkContext that can read the save object file.

Re: Implement saveAsTextFile() in the RDD class

Ryan Hafen Thanks for your comment. As Sun Rui said, making `saveAsTextFile` mimic the Spark function was the goal of this PR.
Regarding the `saveAsObjectFile`, there are a couple of ways we could go about implementing this

1. I think your point about supporting a sequenceFile would be good to have, but it is tricky as full support for sequence file requires being able to serialize and deserialize Hadoop writable types (this should soon be possible if we better conversions from R types to Java types as described in SPARKR-145)

2. However, I think your use case doesn't really require general purpose sequenceFile from what I can see. The RRDDs we have in SparkR are already serialized using R's serializer and saved as Array[Byte] on Java side. It should be pretty simple to save out these Array[Byte] as object files and then support loading them back in using SparkR. Let me know if this will work for your use case and I'll add some more implementation details to SPARKR-146
